title: jev ask returns http_400 for the question shape its own --help advertises
body:
## What happens

`jev ask` returns `http_400` when the questions are sent in the first of the two shapes its own help text advertises. `jev --help` says:

```
ask    raw Jev call: {"state": ..., "questions": [{"id","kind","text"}]} or a mapping of
       name -> {type: choice|score|noul, instructions, criteria}
```

The list form fails. The mapping form that the same line describes goes through.

## Repro

```console
$ echo '{"state":"The diff adds a null check and one unit test. No integration tests were run.","questions":[{"id":"merge","kind":"noul","text":"Is the evidence sufficient to merge this change?"}]}' | jev ask
{
  "error": "http_400"
}

$ echo '{"state":"The diff adds a null check and one unit test. No integration tests were run.","questions":{"merge":{"type":"noul","instructions":"Is the evidence sufficient to merge this change?"}}}' | jev ask
{
  "answers": {
    "merge": {
      "type": "noul",
      "noul": 0.22
    }
  },
  "usage": { ... }
}
```

## Cause

`cmd_ask` normalises the list into a mapping, but the only key it removes is `id`:

```python
questions = {str(q.get("id") or f"q{position + 1}"): {k: v for k, v in q.items() if k != "id"} ...}
```

So the body that actually leaves the process is:

```json
{"merge": {"kind": "noul", "text": "Is the evidence sufficient?"}}
```

The API schema takes `type` and `instructions` (the Choice / Score / Noul primitive pages), so `kind` and `text` are names only the help text uses. The server rejects the body before judging anything:

```
Invalid decision request. Send only model, state, and bounded typed questions
```

0.13.2 fixed the crash on this shape ("`jev ask` crashed on the shape its own help text suggests") by accepting the list, but the vocabulary was never translated, so the `AttributeError` became a 400. The mapping path through `client.ask` is unaffected — it is only the list path that is broken.

## Why the test suite does not catch it

`AskQuestionShapeTests` mocks `cli.client.ask`, so nothing checks what the process puts on the wire, and one assertion pins the spelling the API rejects:

```python
self.assertEqual(questions["q1"]["kind"], "score")
```

## Suggested fix

```python
_ALIASES = {"kind": "type", "text": "instructions"}
...
{_ALIASES.get(k, k): v for k, v in q.items() if k != "id"}
```

plus changing that assertion to `questions["q1"]["type"]` and asserting `instructions`, which pins the vocabulary without a network call.

## Where I saw it

0.13.2, main `04d41ff`. I hit it through the Experiential Labs gateway (`POST https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/systemone`, free-tier key), which serves the same System One shape; that key returns 401 against `api.typesafe.ai`, so I could not exercise the TypeSafe host directly. The body `cmd_ask` builds is identical and the response is a body-validation error rather than an auth error.

title: Routing cache key omits context size; compaction batches by count, not bytes
body:
Hi — reviewing this for a write-up. Two things first, because they're the reason I read the whole repository: the injection question in `rerank.py` is the only one I've seen that names exfiltration-by-rendered-image, and `jev-compaction` ships an eval showing the feature makes handoffs worse, then defaults it off and writes that into the docstring. Publishing a negative result about your own headline feature is rare and worth saying out loud.

Two bugs, both reproduced against a local stand-in at `a5d8901`.

**1. The routing cache key omits the context size, so a cached decision can overflow the window it was not sized for.**

`route.py:420`:

```python
material = "\x00".join([ask, str(profile), str(only_provider), str(has_images), str(pinned), POLICY_VERSION])
```

and the lookup at `:487` returns before `_pick()` runs, so the context-fit check at `:352` and the sticky-context guard at `:549` are both skipped on a hit.

Reproduced with a stand-in answering "trivial" and a `simple` tier whose model has a 32k window:

```
1st call, context 1,000 tokens   -> cheap/tiny-v1   cached None
2nd call, context 300,000 tokens -> cheap/tiny-v1   cached True
what _pick would return at 300k  -> None
```

With `cache_repeat_asks` off, the same second call correctly returns `mid/general-v2` with "no simple model fits this turn".

The trigger is ordinary: any repeated short instruction — a cron turn, "continue", a templated prompt — seen first in a small context and again once the session has grown. README line 102 ("A large context never switches to a cheaper model mid-session") holds only on a miss. Adding a coarse context bucket to the key would fix it; the same key also omits the config, so editing `tiers` has no effect until the process restarts.

**2. `compact.py` batches by turn count, so a CJK conversation loses whole batches — and reports `ok`.**

`compact.py:55` splits on `BATCH = 40` turns. `rerank.py:476` already has a byte-aware packer, and its docstring is exactly this problem:

> Counting passages is not enough. The client measures the JSON-encoded state, and a non-Latin character encodes to six, so sixty Japanese passages were several times over the limit and every such shortlist failed open as state_too_large.

Compaction never got that. 40 turns × `TURN_CHARS = 700` × 6 bytes ≈ 168,000 against `MAX_STATE_CHARS = 60_000`. Measured on a mixed transcript:

```
state chars for one 40-turn batch = 180441   (limit 60000)
status: ok   jev_calls: 1   errors: ['state_too_large']   counts: {'keep': 42, 'summarize': 40, 'drop': 0}
```

The second part is what makes it silent: `compact.py:78` computes `"status": "ok" if calls or not judged`, so one successful batch masks the failed ones. Those 40 turns sit at the fail-open default of `summarize` and get clipped to 400 characters in the digest — while `jev-compaction/SKILL.md:64` tells the agent to use the plain transcript on `fail_open`, which it never sees. Reusing `_pack()` and reporting `partial` when any batch errors would cover both halves.

**Smaller, all checked:**

- `route.py:492` runs the risk-word check on the already-clipped `ask` (625 head + 1875 tail), so a destructive instruction in the middle of a long turn does not trip the guard on line 101 of the README. I confirmed with an 11,957-character prompt: present in the full text, absent from what is sent.
- `jev-skill-select/SKILL.md:13` says "two requests". The code sends `ceil(N/120) + 1`, so the 377 skills in your README are five requests, per turn. Round trips and billed requests aren't the same thing and the difference is most of a session's cost.
- README line 87 says routing is "capped at 3,000 characters"; `route.py:53` is `ask_chars: 2500`.
- The redactor passes a bare card number, a patient line, a CRM id and an internal IP — I ran each through `privacy.redact` and `is_sensitive`. That is a fair scope for regexes, but the plugin injects "never send Jev credentials, customer data or anything marked private" into the agent's system prompt at `__init__.py:345`, and automatic routing in the default `redacted-text` mode gives the agent no way to comply. Worth a line in the README next to the mode table.

**CI has been red for eight consecutive runs**, including the tag builds for v0.13.0, v0.13.1 and v0.13.2, on a real bug rather than flakiness: `jev_gui_agent.py:855` and `:951` bind `opener=subprocess.run` as a default argument at import, so `mock.patch.object(gui.subprocess, "run", ...)` in `tests/test_gui_agent.py:607` never takes effect and `main()` shells out to `/usr/bin/open`. Three failures on Linux; on macOS I'd expect those tests to "pass" by actually opening System Settings, though I only have Linux to check on. Taking `opener` from a module-level name instead of a default argument would fix it.

Happy to send a PR for any of these.

title: Plugin routing silently dead: `_on_llm_request` registers against hook name not in `VALID_HOOKS`
body:
## Bug Description

After installing the plugin via `install.py` on Hermes Agent (2026-09-20, `~/hermes-jev-skills-review/`), the model-routing shadow mode is silently a no-op. `pre_llm_call` registers, but the function that actually calls `route.decide()` and writes to `~/.hermes/logs/jev-decisions.jsonl` is `_on_llm_request`, which registers against a hook name that does not exist in this Hermes Agent version's `VALID_HOOKS` set.

The registration silently fails (debug-level log only) and the plugin's primary function (model routing + decision logging) does nothing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install: `git clone https://github.com/kerpopule/hermes-jev-skills.git ~/hermes-jev-skills-review && python3 ~/hermes-jev-skills-review/install.py`
2. Ensure key wired: `jev setup-key` (or `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` env)
3. Set shadow mode: write `{"routing":"shadow"}` to `~/.hermes/jev/state.json`
4. Restart the Hermes Agent gateway
5. Send a fresh turn (Discord, TUI, dashboard — any path that runs the agent loop)
6. Inspect `~/.hermes/logs/jev-decisions.jsonl`

## Expected Behavior

A JSONL decision log entry appears: `{"ts":..., "kind":"route", "mode":"shadow", "from":"<provider>:<model>", "routed": true/false, "model":..., "tier":..., ...}`.

## Actual Behavior

`~/.hermes/logs/jev-decisions.jsonl` is **never created**. No routing decisions are logged.

## Root Cause

`plugins/hermes-jev/__init__.py` declares three hook callbacks at lines 358-359:

```python
ctx.register_hook("pre_llm_call", _on_pre_llm_call)
ctx.register_hook("transform_llm_output", _on_transform_output)
```

…and `plugin.yaml` advertises `provides_hooks: [pre_llm_call, transform_llm_output]` — but the **`_on_llm_request`** function that does the actual work (lines 163–210) is NEVER registered against any hook. It's the only function that:

- reads `_setting("routing", "shadow")` 
- calls `route.decide(...)` 
- invokes `_log({"kind":"route", ...})` to write `jev-decisions.jsonl`

Looking at the runtime side: `hermes_cli/plugins.py:108-130` defines `VALID_HOOKS`, and `llm_request` is not in it. The closest valid hooks are `pre_api_request` and `post_api_request` (line 117). The plugin's `plugin.yaml` also lies — it advertises `llm_request` in `provides_hooks` even though the runtime never had such a hook.

`_on_pre_llm_call` (the one that IS registered) only fires when `state.json` has `"skills": "on"` and never writes routing logs.

## Suggested Fix

Either:
1. **Plugin side** — register `_on_llm_request` against `pre_api_request` (which is in VALID_HOOKS at plugins.py:117). Adapt the kwargs since `pre_api_request` passes `provider`, `model`, `messages`, etc., not the `request` dict shape the current `_on_llm_request` expects.
2. **Runtime side** — add `llm_request` to `VALID_HOOKS` and implement the dispatch path in the agent loop (likely `run_agent.py` or `agent/turn_context.py`). This is the cleaner long-term fix since the agent loop already has a `transform_request` seam.

## Verification Done on This Host

- `mgr._hooks["pre_llm_call"]` correctly shows 1 callback (`_on_pre_llm_call`) — that hook IS registered.
- `mgr._hooks["transform_llm_output"]` correctly shows 1 callback.
- `mgr._hooks["llm_request"]` does not exist; calling `mgr.iter_hook_callbacks("llm_request")` raises (name not in registry).
- `invoke_hook("pre_llm_call", user_message="hello there short test turn from mark", model="openai-codex:gpt-6-astra", ...)` returns 0 results — the registered `_on_pre_llm_call` short-circuits at `if _setting("skills", "off") != "on"`.
- After gateway restart + real Discord turn, `~/.hermes/logs/jev-decisions.jsonl` is not created.

## Environment

- `hermes-agent` checkout: `/home/dejjem/.hermes/hermes-agent/`
- Plugin: `~/.hermes/plugins/hermes-jev/` (the kerpopule fork, not the built-in)
- `jev` CLI: 0.18.0 (after `install.py` upgrade)
- OS: Linux 6.18.39+rpt-rpi-v8 (Debian bookworm, headless RPi)
- Hermes Agent dashboard gateway runs at :9119 / :8642 / :8644; Discord adapter connected as Hermes#8294

## Impact

- Routing shadow mode does nothing — no log, no decisions.
- Skill suggestion path (via `_on_pre_llm_call`) works only when `state.json` has `skills: "on"`, which is a separate opt-in.
- Compaction / memory filter / supervise / escalate tools (registered as agent tools) still work — those don't depend on the broken hook.

## Workaround

Until upstream fix lands, the `state.json` setting is harmless but inert. Users wanting the routing-log behaviour would need to either:
- Add a `pre_api_request` callback adapter that mirrors `_on_llm_request`, or
- Patch `hermes_cli/plugins.py` to add `llm_request` to `VALID_HOOKS` AND wire dispatch in `run_agent.py` at the `transform_request` seam.

(Workaround not applied here; filing for upstream awareness.)

title: Match the indent of entries already in plugins.enabled
body:
A Hermes `config.yaml` writes its `plugins.enabled` items with four spaces. The
installer inserted its own entries with two, so a list that already held plugins
ended up with mixed indents in one block. YAML folds the deeper lines into the
line above instead of raising, and the whole tail became a single scalar:

```
before -> ['hermes-handoff', 'hermes-jev - api2tg - hermes_otel - ponytail']
after  -> ['hermes-handoff', 'hermes-jev', 'api2tg', 'hermes_otel', 'ponytail']
```

`api2tg`, `hermes_otel` and `ponytail` stopped loading, with no error raised and a
successful install report. Found by installing 0.18.0 into a live Hermes profile
that already had three plugins enabled.

The fix copies the indent of the entries already in the list, and keeps two
spaces for the empty-list and missing-section cases. `tests/test_install.py`
adds `test_deeper_item_indent_is_matched`, which fails on the old code and
passes on the new one; the other 30 installer tests are unchanged and pass.

title: 0.19.0: Jev through Venice, which prices the decision model at zero
body:
Adds Venice as a third provider, alongside TypeSafe and OpenRouter.

Venice serves the same decision model itself, as its own modality rather than a text model:
`GET /models?type=decision` returns `jev-latest`, named **"Jev (System One)"**, priced **0 usd / 0 diem**, reached at `POST /api/v1/decisions`. Note it is *not* callable through `/chat/completions` — that answers `404 Specified model not found` — and `type=text` omits it entirely, so only `type=all` or `type=decision` surfaces it.

## Verified live, all three question shapes

```
choice -> {'choice': 'billing', 'probabilities': {'billing': 1.0, 'technical': 0.0}, 'confidence': 1.0}
score  -> {'score': 0.04, 'probabilities': {'0': 0.97, '1': 0.03, '2': 0.0}, 'confidence': 0.94}
noul   -> {'noul': 0.39}
```

The `score` case is the interesting one: the state was a passage about crates being rebuilt and the gate passing, and the question asked whether it was relevant to a Blender texture problem. 0.97 on "irrelevant" is the right answer, not a coin flip.

## Venice is appended last, deliberately

It is currently free, which makes it tempting to prefer and exactly why it should not be. An install already resolving through TypeSafe or OpenRouter keeps routing where it did; a machine holding **both** an OpenRouter and a Venice key still resolves to OpenRouter. `test_venice_is_last_so_a_machine_with_both_keys_never_reroutes` asserts it.

## One limit, stated in the CHANGELOG

Venice answers a `choice` with more than 255 criteria with `Too many choices. Must have at most 255 choices.` A 430-item option set needs shortlisting first.

## Sync rule

- 3 tests in `tests/test_jevkit.py`, mirroring the existing provider tests
- `CHANGELOG.md` entry; `skills/jev-setup/SKILL.md` offers the new provider; `README.md` mentions it
- `jevkit/__init__.py` and `hermes/plugin/hermes-jev/plugin.yaml` bumped together to 0.19.0

## A note on one rule I had to fix in my own patch

My first version bound the transport and model into module-level tables. That is the trap CONTRIBUTING.md warns about — patching the module afterwards would have done nothing — so both now resolve at call time from the globals.

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → 772 tests, and `python3 scripts/check_release.py` → clean (92 text files). Locally on Windows I see 19 failures / 9 errors, all pre-existing and all Windows-only (`WinError`, `WindowsPath`, `PermissionError`); pristine upstream shows the identical 28, so this patch adds none.

title: 0.19.0: jev from anywhere, not only from inside the checkout
body:
Fixes a Windows launcher bug that makes `jev` unusable from every directory except the checkout.

## The bug

`bin/jev` put the checkout on the interpreter's search path like this:

```sh
PYTHONPATH="$here${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" exec python3 -m jevkit "$@"
```

Two Windows problems in one line:

1. `$here` is a **shell** path. Under git-bash it is `/c/Users/Ted/hermes-jev-skills`, which a
   native Python (python.org 3.14 here) does not resolve — it looks under `C:\` instead.
2. `PYTHONPATH` separates with **`;`** on Windows, not `:`. Prepending with `:` therefore did not
   add an entry — it made the whole variable a single unparseable path, so even an
   already-correct `PYTHONPATH` was thrown away.

Net effect: `jev` worked only when the working directory happened to be the checkout, because
`python -m` falls back to the cwd.

```
$ cd ~            # anywhere that is not the checkout
$ jev --version
C:\...\python.exe: No module named jevkit
```

This matters beyond the CLI: cron jobs and agent shells invoke `jev` from their own working
directories, so any of them calling it was failing. The Hermes plugin is unaffected — the
installer bundles its own copy of `jevkit` inside the plugin — which is exactly why the bug is
easy to miss.

## The fix

Run from the checkout, which puts `jevkit` on `sys.path` with no path translation and no
dependence on the caller's environment:

```sh
cd "$here" || exit 1
exec python3 -m jevkit "$@"
```

I chose this over `cygpath -w` plus a `;`-aware separator because it is two lines, needs no new
dependency, and behaves identically on Linux and macOS. If you would rather keep `PYTHONPATH` and
translate the path, I am happy to redo it that way — say which you prefer.

## Evidence

```
before, from $HOME:              No module named jevkit        (exit 1)
after,  from $HOME:              jev --version -> 0.19.0      (exit 0)
after,  from a third directory:  jev doctor -> provider venice, reachable: true, 1012 ms
```

## The test

One test in `tests/test_install.py`, next to the existing link and "stays runnable" tests. It runs
the launcher from an unrelated directory **with `PYTHONPATH` removed from the environment** — that
half matters, because a `PYTHONPATH` that happens to carry the checkout hides this bug completely,
which may be why it survived.

```
python -m unittest tests.test_install.LauncherRunsFromAnywhereTests -v   ->  Ran 1 test, OK
python -m unittest discover -s tests        ->  770 tests, failures=19, errors=9
python scripts/check_release.py             ->  clean (92 text files)
```

Pre-existing on this box: 769 tests and the same 19 failures / 9 errors on untouched `main`
(Windows-only: `WinError`, `WindowsPath`, `PermissionError`). This PR adds one test and no failures.

## Sync rule

Test + `CHANGELOG.md` + both version files (`jevkit/__init__.py` and
`hermes/plugin/hermes-jev/plugin.yaml`) bumped together to 0.19.0.

**Note on versioning:** #6 also bumps to 0.19.0 (the Venice provider). They are independent, so
whichever lands second should become 0.19.1 — happy to rebase mine once you say which order you
want them in.

title: install.py corrupts plugins.enabled when the existing list uses Hermes's own 4-space indent (a pre-existing plugin silently stops loading)
body:
### What happened, and what you expected instead

`python3 install.py` rewrote `~/.hermes/config.yaml` so that a plugin which was already in
`plugins.enabled` **before** the install is no longer in it. No error, no warning, exit status 0,
and the file still parses.

Before:

```yaml
plugins:
  enabled:
    - hermes-lcm
```

After:

```yaml
plugins:
  enabled:
  - hermes-handoff
  - hermes-jev
    - hermes-lcm
```

That is valid YAML, so nothing complains — it just means something different:

```
$ hermes config get plugins.enabled
- hermes-handoff
- hermes-jev - hermes-lcm
```

`hermes-lcm` has been absorbed into a single string with the item above it, so it is no longer
enabled and stops loading on the next gateway start. I expected the install to add
`hermes-handoff` and `hermes-jev` and leave `hermes-lcm` exactly where it was.

Recovered with:

```bash
hermes config set plugins.enabled '["hermes-handoff","hermes-jev","hermes-lcm"]'
```

### The smallest way to see it again

Calling your own `enable_plugins` — nothing else is needed:

```python
import sys, tempfile, yaml
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, "<repo>")
import install

d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); cfg = d / "config.yaml"
cfg.write_text("plugins:\n  enabled:\n    - hermes-lcm\n  disabled: []\n")
install.enable_plugins(cfg, ["hermes-handoff", "hermes-jev"], True)
print(cfg.read_text())
print(yaml.safe_load(cfg.read_text())["plugins"]["enabled"])
```

```
plugins:
  enabled:
  - hermes-handoff
  - hermes-jev
    - hermes-lcm
  disabled: []
['hermes-handoff', 'hermes-jev - hermes-lcm']      # hermes-lcm is gone
```

The same call against a 2-space list is correct:

```
plugins:
  enabled:
  - hermes-handoff
  - hermes-jev
  - hermes-lcm
['hermes-handoff', 'hermes-jev', 'hermes-lcm']      # fine
```

**The trigger is the indent of the items already in the list.** `install.py:216` inserts at a
hard-coded two spaces:

```python
block.insert(key + 1, f"  - {name}")
```

`hermes config set` writes list items with four (`    - name`). The new two-space line lands
immediately above the existing four-space one, and that line's extra leading spaces make it a
*continuation* of the previous item rather than a new sequence entry — so two plugin names
become one scalar. Anyone who has added a plugin with `hermes config` rather than editing the
file by hand is in the four-space shape and hits this on their first install.

The `already enabled` check on line 206-207 uses `^\s*-\s*` and so matches either indent,
which is why a re-run does not repair it: the corrupted entry no longer matches the name it
replaced, and the surviving four-space line is never normalised.

A fix that removes the whole class of bug: read the indent from the items already in the
block (fall back to two when the list is empty) instead of assuming one.

### Output of `jev doctor`

```json
{
  "version": "0.18.0",
  "key": { "present": true, "provider": "typesafe", "source": "environment", "length": 107 },
  "jev": { "reachable": true, "latency_ms": 726 },
  "hermes_home": "/home/theredpanda/.hermes"
}
```

### Version

0.18.0 (commit 29e64b57026eb040b355c260a2480015bd459611)

### Where it runs

Hermes

### OS and Python version

WSL2 (Ubuntu) on Windows 11, Python 3.11.15

---

Found by an agent installing this repo following `AGENTS.md`. Everything else in the install
went exactly as documented — this was the only thing that needed a second look, and it took a
`hermes config get` afterwards to notice at all.

title: fix: keep a plugin list's own indentation when enabling plugins
body:
## What this changes

`enable_plugins` writes new entries as `  - name`, assuming a 2-space list. When the
existing list is indented deeper, YAML reads the sequence as **one scalar with the deeper
items folded into it** — the plugins already in the file are silently dropped. The fix
follows the list's own indentation, falling back to 2 spaces only when the list is empty.

## Why

I was reviewing this repo before installing it (the SkillSpector gate here is noisy, so I
read the code instead), and `install.py --check` looked clean. What it cannot tell you is
what the config looks like *after* the edit, so I ran `enable_plugins` against a copy of my
own config. Mine is written with 4-space items — that is what `hermes` itself emits when it
rewrites `plugins.enabled`:

```yaml
plugins:
  enabled:
    - herdr-agent-state
    - memory-wiki
    - orca-status
```

After enabling, that became:

```yaml
plugins:
  enabled:
  - hermes-handoff
  - hermes-jev
    - herdr-agent-state
    - memory-wiki
    - orca-status
```

which parses as `['hermes-handoff', 'hermes-jev - herdr-agent-state - memory-wiki - orca-status']`.
Four of five plugins gone. `install.py` exits 0, reports both as `enabled`, and
`--check`'s output is identical either way — the loss surfaces the next time one of those
plugins is needed, with a backup on disk nobody knows to restore. `--uninstall` is hit too:
its `del block[i]` no longer matches the folded lines.

A real config, not a hypothetical: the 4-space form is what the config in front of me had,
and the two-space form is what your `CONFIG` fixture has — which is exactly why the suite
was green.

## How it was checked

- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passes — **795 tests OK** (23.1s)
- [x] `python3 scripts/check_release.py` is clean — `clean: 96 text files`
- [x] A test that fails before this change and passes after:
      `ConfigEditTests::test_an_indented_list_keeps_its_own_indent`. With the old line
      restored it fails with
      `AssertionError: 'coagent-observer' not found in ['hermes-handoff', 'hermes-jev - coagent-observer - other-plugin']`,
      and passes after. Verified by temporarily reverting the one-line change, not by
      reading it.
- [x] Ran it against real Jev, or explained why that was not possible — **not applicable**:
      this is config-file editing only, no Jev call in the path. `enable_plugins` is a pure
      text edit.

Both new tests assert on the **parsed** list, never on the text. The broken and the correct
output differ by two spaces of indentation, which is why a text assertion (and the existing
`test_enable_and_disable_touch_only_the_list`) does not see it. `test_a_2_space_list_still_round_trips`
covers the shape that already worked, so the fix follows rather than replaces.

## The two things reviewers will look at first

- [x] **Nothing new leaves the machine.** No network call, no new URL, no new request path.
      `git diff main...HEAD | grep -E '^\+' | grep -iE 'http|url|request|socket|urllib|token'`
      is empty.
- [x] **It fails open.** No new `raise`, no new `assert` in production code — the diff adds
      two assignments and one interpolation. When a config cannot be read or written the
      existing behaviour is untouched.

## Notes

`parse_plugin_list` in the test file is stdlib-only on purpose. The repo keeps a
no-dependencies promise and PyYAML is a dashboard extra, so the test reads the one YAML rule
the text edit can break (sequence indentation) rather than pulling in a parser.

Diff is 12 lines in `install.py` and 69 in the test file.

title: fix(skillpick): read a description written as a YAML block scalar
body:
## What this changes

`_front_matter` read a front-matter key by splitting its own line at the first colon and stopping. A description written as `description: >` (or `|`) with the text indented underneath — valid YAML, and the only readable way to write several sentences — came back as the marker itself, `">"`. The skill then reached Jev with no description at all and could only be picked for what its name already said.

## Why

I was measuring `jev pick-skill` against turns whose right answer I already knew, on a catalog of 34 skills. A web-research skill whose description names every platform it covers (`小红书`, Reddit, GitHub, RSS, …) was passed over for a link I shared; Jev picked a browser skill at 0.50 instead. It was not a ranking problem. Six of the 34 — the six whose descriptions are longest and most specific, four of them written in Chinese — had `>` for a description.

With the block read, the same turn picks the right skill at **0.95**, and three other turns that had gone to a plausible-but-wrong neighbour land on the right skill at 0.96–0.98.

30 of 535 `SKILL.md` files under `~/.claude/plugins` on this machine write their description this way, so it is not a local habit. It also fits what `0.16.0` already found the hard way: a description the picker cannot read is a skill that cannot be found, and the fix belongs in the description path, not in a threshold.

## How it was checked

- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passes — **803 passed, 1 skipped** (799 + the 4 added by the follow-up commit)
- [x] `python3 scripts/check_release.py` is clean
- [x] A test that fails before this change and passes after: `FrontMatterTests` — `test_a_folded_description_is_read_not_left_as_its_marker`, `test_a_literal_description_is_read_the_same_way`, `test_a_blank_line_inside_a_block_does_not_end_it`, `test_a_skill_with_only_a_marker_for_a_description_is_still_dropped`. All four fail on `main`; the other two in the class are regression guards and are green both ways.
- [x] Ran it against real Jev — a 34-skill catalog, `jev pick-skill`, the numbers above. The router this fixes has since been serving every turn on a 50-skill machine for a day, pinned to `jev-1.13.0`.
- [x] **CI matrix reproduced locally**, because no checks have run on this fork PR (`gh pr checks` reports none). Both legs of your Python matrix plus the version in between: **3.9.25 → 803 passed / 1 skipped**, **3.12.3 → same**, **3.13.12 → same**; `scripts/check_release.py` clean on 3.13. Linux only — I cannot run the macOS leg.

### Follow-up commit `2d5159a`

The first commit was still wrong and its own tests did not catch it. `_BLOCK_SCALARS` was a fixed set of eight strings, but YAML lets the indentation and chomping indicators appear in either order, so `>2-`, `|+2`, `>-2` and `|2+` are all valid headers it missed — and it compared the whole remainder of the line, so `description: > # folded` missed too. An unrecognised header falls through to the plain `key: value` branch, which is the exact bug this PR is about.

It now matches the shape (`^[>|][0-9+-]*\s*(?:#.*)?$`) and ends a block on the first non-blank line less indented than the block's own first line, rather than on the next line that happens to contain a colon.

Four tests added, all red against `bede886` (7 subtest failures):

- `test_an_indent_and_chomping_indicator_together_is_still_a_block` (subtests `>2-`, `|+2`, `>-2`, `|2+`)
- `test_a_comment_after_the_header_does_not_hide_the_block`
- `test_a_less_indented_line_ends_the_block`
- `test_a_literal_block_with_both_indicators_is_normalised_to_one_line`

One deliberate choice worth flagging: `|` is normalised to a single line like `>`, not kept with its breaks. Strict YAML would keep them, but both go to the same consumer, which truncates the description to a few hundred characters and lists it for a decision model — the author's line breaks carry nothing the reader can use, and `>` already folds blank lines away in this implementation. A test pins that so it is a decision rather than an accident; happy to switch it if you would rather be YAML-exact.

Both commits are left on the branch rather than squashed, so the failure mode is visible if that is useful; squash on merge if not.

## The two things reviewers will look at first

- [x] **Nothing new leaves the machine.** No new field and no new call. The same `description[:200]` / `[:600]` goes to Jev as before; it now contains the description the skill's author wrote instead of one punctuation mark. A skill whose description was already on one line is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [x] **It fails open.** No new exception path. `_front_matter` still returns a plain dict and never raises on malformed input; a block with no body yields an empty description, which `discover()` drops exactly as it dropped a missing one. A key following a block is still read (there is a test for that, green on `main` too).

## Notes

Folded (`>`) and literal (`|`) blocks are both joined with spaces. A literal block's newlines are meaningful in YAML, but this text is truncated to 200 or 600 characters and handed to a decision model, so they carry nothing — flattening both keeps one code path. Say the word if you would rather `|` kept its newlines.

Indentation indicators (`>2`, `|2`) are accepted as markers but their explicit indent is not honoured; the block still ends at the first non-blank unindented line, which is right for every real front matter I have seen.
